owner_steps.title: Review the plan and give the go-ahead
owner_steps.what: Read this package, answer the decisions you want changed (silence on a routine batch counts as approval), and give the go-ahead for execution in the conversation.
owner_steps.why: Execution starts only on your go-ahead, given on the merged plan; every decision listed here was taken on your behalf and is reviewed by you before anything is changed.

owner_steps.title: Grant push access to your private datasheets repository
owner_steps.what: Confirm that the Claude GitHub App may write (push) to hundertvolt/datasheets, not only read it, so the executing session can create its main branch and push the 21 datasheet PDFs there.
owner_steps.why: You decided to move the datasheets out of the public repository into that private one, included as a submodule. Only reading it has been checked so far. Without push access the move and its two documentation sections are skipped and nothing is removed from the repository; the rest of the plan is unaffected.
owner_steps.when: before unit U28 (asked again at U28's start if not yet confirmed)

owner_steps.title: Decide on GitHub secret scanning for the repository
owner_steps.what: If the one-time scan of the whole git history finds GitHub's secret scanning switched off for the repository, decide whether to switch it on. It is a repository setting, which the executor never changes.
owner_steps.why: The history scan reports what GitHub itself sees. Switching the setting on is a forward guard for a public repository, but it is your setting.
owner_steps.when: after unit U29, shown again in the end-of-execution review

owner_steps.title: Give a go-ahead in each hardware session's own conversation
owner_steps.what: Nothing touches the dev board, the bench Pi or the bench network until you say so in that session's conversation. A go-ahead does not carry over to another conversation; once given it covers the rest of that conversation. Name in the go-ahead any optional item you want included (removing stale bench packages, the fresh-bridge proof, the hotspot-settle check).
owner_steps.why: The standing CLAUDE.md rule for real hardware. All hardware work is collected into three sessions after the last software unit, so you give at most three go-aheads.
owner_steps.when: phase C, after unit U37: sessions 1, 2 and 3

owner_steps.title: Confirm two bench facts at the start of the first session
owner_steps.what: Confirm whether the router's DHCP reservation for the bench Pi is keyed to eth0's own MAC address, and whether the BME688 on GP16/GP17 is still attached.
owner_steps.why: Both are recorded in the bench facts; neither can be read reliably by a script.

owner_steps.title: Be at the bench for the operator round
owner_steps.what: Confirm the round's write budget before it starts, then do the hands-on steps: write down the rig geometry, unplug and replug the SCD30 and the FRAM, short SDA to ground, power-cycle and cut power at the planned points, open the website on your phones and desktop browsers (Safari on macOS and iOS, Chrome and Firefox on Android, desktop Chromium and Firefox), and compare the four field units' device files with the physical units without flashing or connecting them. Bring an oscilloscope only if you want the two held-SDA rows measured; without one they stay owed, never guessed.
owner_steps.why: These rows need a person, a real phone or physical access. The write budget (2 flash writes and 2 SCD30 NVM writes for the persistence steps, up to 60 scratch writes for the power-cut test, the reset-to-defaults power cut's deletions and restores) is stated before you start, and any step that would spend more stops for you.
owner_steps.when: phase C, session 1, round R2 (after the first clean default run)

owner_steps.title: Keep the board free for the 12.4-day rollover run
owner_steps.what: Either keep the first session's conversation open as its tail, or open a new conversation whose go-ahead names the rollover round to read the result. During the window nothing else may use the board.
owner_steps.why: The run proves the device across the 2**30-millisecond tick wrap on silicon. If a later fix changes tick-handling code, you decide whether the run is repeated.
owner_steps.when: phase C, session 2 (after the soak round)

owner_steps.title: Agree to close the hardware phase and to merge
owner_steps.what: Two agreements at the end: that the hardware phase is complete (this opens phase D), and that the audit is finished, which allows the one merge into main and pushing the release tag. Say also whether the audit branch should be deleted; if you do not name it, it stays.
owner_steps.why: The tag is pushed only with your agreement that the audit is finished; main must be unmoved since the baseline, otherwise you are asked first.
owner_steps.when: end of phase C, then phase D

owner_steps.title: Review the decisions taken during execution
owner_steps.what: A second, shorter review at the end of execution: decisions the executor takes on your behalf while working, held-back dependency updates, parked items and the release version if you have not settled it here. Each comes in your usual question format.
owner_steps.why: Execution never stops to ask; it takes the more conservative, more reversible option and logs it for you. Kept decisions get the tag 'owner-reviewed'; overruled ones go through the normal path, tests first.

hardware_sessions.title: Session 1: bench host, first contact, operator round, wear, soak, reflash
hardware_sessions.rounds: R0, R1, R2, R3, R5, R4 (in that order, one conversation)
hardware_sessions.what_happens: R0 prepares the bench Pi with no board attached: host record, installer checks, the bench tier install, speed probes, the host-side lwIP hammer. R1 makes first contact read-only (status, reset cause, raw FRAM dump, every config file saved), then builds and flashes the dev image and runs the default flash and bench tiers, a few hand-run measurements, and last a deliberate planted red to prove the hardware memory gates fire. R2 is the operator round with you at the bench. R3 runs the opt-in wear tests (persistence writes, a second SCD30 NVM write, the NeoPixel sweep) and ends with the hotspot role-reversal's destructive stage. R5 runs the soaks (1 min, 10 min, 6 h). R4 runs the reflash rows last, because they change the image: the lwIP send-stall pair (unpatched control image first, then the fix), the CRC16 UART run and the reflash smoke test, and restores the standard image.
hardware_sessions.owner_present: Go-ahead in the conversation; at the bench in person for R2; two confirmations in R0.
hardware_sessions.duration: Not estimated in the plan. The 6-hour soak alone takes six hours; the full bench tier took 41 minutes in its last recorded run, before the flash tier, the lower test levels and the gated runs. Expect at least a long day.
hardware_sessions.wear_or_risk: Flash writes only behind their markers and stated in each round's plan: R1 the image flash plus 2-3 pinned prerequisite writes and at most 1 SCD30 NVM write; R2 as in its budget; R3 the README budget table's sum for the flags used; R4 5 flash cycles (7 if the hotspot-settle row is planned); R5 none. Risks: the role reversal's stage 6 permanently deactivates the board's Wi-Fi (recovered over USB, named before it runs); every bench-network change runs under the dead-man's switch; Erase FRAM overwrites the FRAM logs, so they are saved first.

hardware_sessions.title: Session 2: the 12.4-day tick rollover
hardware_sessions.what_happens: On the release-candidate image, a detached run on the bench Pi polls the board hourly over REST until its uptime passes the 2**30 ms tick wrap plus an hour, then records a verdict. Started through its own runner, so the result is a recorded clean run.
hardware_sessions.owner_present: Go-ahead only. It can run as session 1's tail if that conversation stays open; otherwise a new go-ahead naming R6 reads the result.
hardware_sessions.duration: About 12.4 days plus an hour of margin; the board is used by nothing else in that window.
hardware_sessions.wear_or_risk: No wear. The bench network switch is armed only across the start-up fixtures.

hardware_sessions.title: Session 3: the release proof
hardware_sessions.what_happens: Only after every hardware finding is fixed and one full re-verification pass is green: a throwaway image without the boot-time gc.threshold line runs the full default flash and bench tiers with zero memory-allocation markers, then the release image from the final commit runs them again. Every reset seen across the rounds is attributed; the board ends on the release image in its standard state.
hardware_sessions.owner_present: Go-ahead; afterwards you are told the hardware phase is complete and asked for the agreement that opens phase D.
hardware_sessions.duration: Not estimated in the plan: two full default runs, plus a 6-hour soak again if the tree changed since session 1.
hardware_sessions.wear_or_risk: 2 image flashes plus the two default runs' pinned prerequisite writes.

decisions.title: The release is version 2.0
decisions.decision: The firmware and website ship as version 2.0: today's pre-release 2.0b0 without its beta marker. The tag on the final merge is v2.0.
decisions.why: No owner row sets the number. You asked for a true release version, and the project's own version scheme reads 2.0b0's release as 2.0.
decisions.if_no: You name the number; it lives in one place, and the tag and release note follow it.

decisions.title: The concrete spelling of every REST and config key
decisions.decision: You decided on one key scheme, with the new API as the reference. The planning chose the spelling: setting and value keys in PascalCase, acronyms upper-case, the full words Interval and Offset, 'Pres' for pressure, and no unit in a REST key (the unit sits in the field's description). Examples: NTP_Host becomes NTPHost, NTP_Offset_S becomes NTPOffset, Interv becomes FlashInterval, SGPResetVOC becomes ResetVOC, ISLCalibrate becomes Calibrate, lightCmdLED becomes LightCmdLED with R/G/B/T, UtcTime becomes UTCTime. Envelope and section keys stay lowercase, measurement fields keep their names.
decisions.why: Each choice is the form most keys already use; the unit is dropped from keys because only two keys carried one. Every consumer (website, mock, tests, docs) moves in one scripted pass.
decisions.if_no: You name a different rule (for example, keep unit suffixes such as NTPOffset_S); the rename is still one pass, so changing the map now costs nothing extra.
decisions.alternative: keep unit suffixes on REST keys, or camelCase

decisions.title: One REST API reference, frozen at the release
decisions.decision: The REST API (routes, keys, types, units, ranges, result words) gets one reference generated from the code. The mock server, website tests, the twin's PUT matrix and the fifteen places that copy the route list by hand are checked against it or derive from it. From the release on, a stored copy of it fails a check on any unrecorded change, like the stored-config check you already asked for.
decisions.why: Your words were 'the new API is the reference'; today the route set is hand-copied in fifteen test and tool files, seven of which miss a route.
decisions.if_no: The API stays documented by hand and only the stored-config check guards the release; route lists stay hand-kept.

decisions.title: A website left open for days stays healthy and reloads itself after a reflash
decisions.decision: A page left open keeps its memory and timers bounded, updates read-only values in place instead of rebuilding the page every 3 seconds, and after a device reboot or reflash notices the changed build on its next check and reloads itself. The device check runs every 60 s; failed polls back off to at most 60 s.
decisions.why: Today every live section is rebuilt on each poll, and a page open across a reflash keeps polling with a stale script bundle.
decisions.if_no: The page keeps today's rebuild-per-poll and never reloads on its own; you reload by hand after a reflash.
decisions.alternative: show a 'new version, reload' notice instead of reloading

decisions.title: The website meets an accessibility baseline
decisions.decision: Unique ids for every field (numbered by position), every label bound to its control, the closed menu drawer made inert with focus handled, AA contrast in both themes, password inputs styled like other inputs and marked autocomplete='new-password', reduced motion honoured. An automated check in the website tests proves it, written without a new npm dependency.
decisions.why: Gap the planning found against its own quality pillars. The look stays as it is; the colour change you already approved is part of the AA contrast.
decisions.if_no: The website keeps today's markup; only your approved colour change lands.

decisions.title: A confirmation before clearing the DNS fallback list
decisions.decision: The new Clear button for the DNS fallback servers asks the browser's own confirmation ('Clear DNS Fallback Servers?') before it sends the empty value. It is the only dialog on the site; the system commands, including Reset to defaults and Erase FRAM, keep none, as you decided.
decisions.why: Clearing removes every fallback server in one click, and the field has no undo.
decisions.if_no: Clear sends at once, like every other control.

decisions.title: SGP40: a wait time of 0 restores the VOC backup at once
decisions.decision: With WaitTimeNTP = 0 the SGP40 restores its VOC backup immediately at boot, without waiting for NTP, rather than never restoring it.
decisions.why: Legacy restores, and its own setting label says '0 = never wait'. Your later work-in-progress code did not restore, which the planning reads as a bug defeating its own intent.
decisions.if_no: 0 means 'no restore', as in the work-in-progress code; a setting of 0 then discards the learned VOC state at every boot.

decisions.title: A failed Apply marks every submitted field Failed
decisions.decision: When an Apply gets no per-field answer back (the request failed), every field it sent is shown as Failed on the page, instead of the failure only being logged.
decisions.why: You see the failure where you made the change; nothing the legacy site did is lost.
decisions.if_no: The page keeps today's behaviour: a failed request is only logged.

decisions.title: Running out of C stack reboots the unit with its own reset reason
decisions.decision: A C-stack overflow caught anywhere is recorded, and the supervisor reboots the unit at its next pass with reset reason 20. The deepest await chain is measured and must stay at most half of the 7,936-byte stack; a host test fails if the chain grows past a pinned depth, and the bench reads the real peak.
decisions.why: A stack overflow is a design defect, not a routine failure; today a broad handler can swallow it and keep running in an unknown state.
decisions.if_no: A stack overflow stays an ordinary caught error; no reset reason 20 and no depth budget.

decisions.title: An unreadable config file is never overwritten
decisions.decision: If a config file exists but cannot be read (I/O error, out of memory), the module runs on its defaults, every PUT to it answers Failed until the next boot, and the file is never rewritten. A readable file with a bad key keeps the one repair per boot.
decisions.why: Today any read failure counts as 'no file' and the file is rewritten with defaults, which loses your settings. Not writing is the conservative choice.
decisions.if_no: An unreadable file is replaced by defaults, as today.
decisions.alternative: serve defaults but allow PUTs to write a fresh file

decisions.title: No timestamps before the first NTP sync
decisions.decision: Until NTP first sets the clock after a boot, readings are published with TS null, and UTCTime/LocalTime read null. Such a reading is a valid measurement, not a failed read. Once set, the clock counts as valid for the rest of the boot, even if a later sync fails.
decisions.why: Before the first sync the clock holds the boot default, so any timestamp would be wrong.
decisions.if_no: Readings carry the board's unsynced clock as their timestamp, as today.

decisions.title: When a reflash erases the stored settings
decisions.decision: The reflash runbook erases the filesystem when a unit moves between the legacy firmware and this one, in either direction. A later update of a unit already on this firmware keeps its stored settings.
decisions.why: Your rule 'erase on every reflash' is read this way because from the release on stored settings are a public interface that a change must migrate; erasing on every update would defeat that.
decisions.if_no: Every reflash erases the settings, and each update means setting the unit up again.

decisions.title: Its own LED pattern when Wi-Fi is switched off for good
decisions.decision: When the unit has permanently deactivated its Wi-Fi after a failed hotspot stage, the Wi-Fi LED blinks 0.1 s on, 2.9 s off: the hotspot pattern inverted, mostly dark, unlike every other state.
decisions.why: That state needs a power cycle to leave and today looks the same as 'disconnected'.
decisions.if_no: The LED stays off in that state, as today.

decisions.title: SCD30 calibration readiness: three new settings with provisional defaults
decisions.decision: Following your four readiness criteria, the SCD30 publishes a readiness code and gains three user settings stored in its config file: noise floor 20 ppm (twice the datasheet repeatability), change-rate limit 10 ppm/min and window 60 s (both provisional until measured on the bench). The SCD30 reader becomes a config-file-backed reader for them; their error log stays RAM-only, as you said 'no extra FRAM chunk'.
decisions.why: You left the values to the bench; these are the starting values, replaced by measured ones in the hardware phase.
decisions.if_no: You name other defaults now, or the bench measurements set them without a provisional value.

decisions.title: Every PUT key gets an answer; unknown keys read Invalid
decisions.decision: A PUT that names an unknown key, an unknown sensor or a malformed sensor entry gets 'Invalid' for it in the per-field result, instead of being silently ignored.
decisions.why: A typo in a key otherwise looks like success.

decisions.title: The audit's merge is the release
decisions.decision: The one merge into main is the release: it carries the version as a git tag and a short release note of user-visible changes against legacy (renamed keys, reset reason, the overnight window, compare-before-write, the new API). The stored-config and REST reference copies are taken from it. The tag is pushed only at the close, with your agreement.
decisions.why: You asked for a true release version; this gives it one defined point that later changes are measured against.
decisions.if_no: The merge happens without a tag or release note, and the reference copies need another anchor.

decisions.title: How the send-stall fix behaves on a stuck connection
decisions.decision: With your send-stall fix (the send returns 'try again' instead of blocking), a connection whose send queue is full retries cooperatively until the peer acknowledges or the 5-second per-call timeout ends it. Load tests bound how much other tasks' latency and CPU share may suffer. If they fail that bound, the fix adds a short wait for 'writable' after each 'try again', and that change is put to you.
decisions.why: This is the smallest patch, the same as the upstream pull request; a full queue with room left turns out to be frequent, so the behaviour is stated and measured rather than assumed.
decisions.if_no: A wait-for-writable back-off is added now, before measuring, which makes the patch larger than upstream's.

decisions.title: The unused humidity helpers are removed
decisions.decision: abs_humidity() and rel_humidity() are removed from the maths helpers, with their tests. If an SHTC3 sensor is ever promoted, it re-adds the legacy formula with its own input checks.
decisions.why: No product code, device or driver uses them; your rule removes unused code. Keeping rel_humidity()'s 0-100 clamp would also break the 'no helper clamps' rule.
decisions.if_no: They stay, with either the legacy clamp as a named exception or returning nothing outside 0-100.

decisions.title: Request heads are capped at 32 headers and 2,048 bytes
decisions.decision: The web server refuses, quietly, a request with more than 32 header lines or a request line and headers over 2,048 bytes in total, before the memory is allocated.
decisions.why: Browsers send about 15-20 headers and curl about 4; the values are estimates, and the operator round measures the longest real head per browser against them.
decisions.if_no: Heads stay unbounded, and a large head can exhaust memory before Microdot's own line check runs.
decisions.alternative: set the limits only after the bench measurement

decisions.title: Static pages are revalidated on every visit
decisions.decision: Static files are served with Cache-Control: no-cache and no ETag, so a browser asks again on every visit.
decisions.why: After a reflash a browser must never show the old page; an ETag would need a hash per file at build time.
decisions.if_no: Browsers may cache pages and show a stale site after a reflash.

decisions.title: Two new status values; four deliberately left out
decisions.decision: /status gains HTTPDropped (requests refused at the connection ceiling, refused for a bad head, or reset early) and WifiTS (when the Wi-Fi snapshot was taken, so a stalled Wi-Fi task shows). Left out, with reasons recorded in the specification: the live open-connection count, the supervisor's task-error budget, and each notification signal's last value and triggered flag.
decisions.why: The two added values make a failure visible that is otherwise only in the history; the four left out are already visible another way or meaningless when read over REST.
decisions.if_no: You name which values to add or drop.

decisions.title: Wi-Fi off for good reads 'not connected' with empty addresses
decisions.decision: When Wi-Fi is permanently deactivated, the networking snapshot reports Mode STA, Connected false, and null for addresses and signal strength, without asking the radio.
decisions.why: The radio is off; reading it would be meaningless, and Connected false is what the device reports today.
decisions.if_no: The fields keep their last values from before the deactivation.

decisions.title: NTPSynced turns false when syncs keep failing
decisions.decision: NTPSynced is true only while the last successful sync is recent: a failed resync no longer resets the staleness count, so a clock that has not synced for several intervals reads as unsynced.
decisions.why: Legacy intended this, but a bug defeated it; your rule says legacy's evident intent counts, not its bug.
decisions.if_no: A failed resync keeps NTPSynced true as today.

decisions.title: No extra origin check on NTP replies
decisions.decision: NTP replies get no originate-timestamp check. Only the configured server's address and port can reach the socket, and each attempt uses a fresh socket, so a late reply to an earlier attempt reaches nothing.
decisions.why: What remains, a host on your network forging the server, is outside the trusted-home-LAN threat model you chose.
decisions.if_no: An originate-timestamp check is added as defence in depth.

decisions.title: The DNS fallback servers become a setting
decisions.decision: The two built-in fallback DNS servers become the NTP setting DNSFallback, default '8.8.8.8,1.1.1.1', up to three IPv4 addresses, empty for none.
decisions.why: You accepted the public fallback as a default value; the NTP client is the only user of the resolver, so the setting lives there.

decisions.title: The hotspot redirects unknown pages to the setup page
decisions.decision: In hotspot mode, a GET for a page that does not exist is answered with a redirect to the device's page, so a phone's captive-portal check opens it.
decisions.why: It is part of the captive portal you already have and adds nothing else.
decisions.if_no: Unknown paths answer 404 in hotspot mode.

decisions.title: One envelope code list; HTTP errors use their status as code
decisions.decision: The response envelope has one code catalog. A shaped HTTP error (400, 404, 405, 413, 500) carries its HTTP status as its envelope code; codes no code path produces are removed.
decisions.why: One list, every code with a producer.
decisions.if_no: Callers may keep inventing their own codes.

decisions.title: The exact words for the two new system commands
decisions.decision: Reset to defaults is sent as SystemCmd 'resetconfig', Erase FRAM as 'erasefram': lowercase, no separator, like 'mempause' and 'bootloader'. Only the exact word works.
decisions.why: You made the exact word the safeguard. 'resetconfig' names what it resets (the config files, not the FRAM logs or the SCD30's memory); neither word is a prefix of another command.

decisions.title: Details of the controlled shutdown sequence
decisions.decision: Any command arriving while a reset is armed is refused; the watchdog latch is set when the command is accepted; reboot and bootloader record reset reasons 3 and 4; an early refusal changes nothing for all four commands; the SCD30's own memory is not among the stores closed during the sequence; the supervisor's own escalation stays direct and re-checks watchdog ownership after its log write.
decisions.why: Each is the more conservative reading of your rules for the sequence and the watchdog takeover.
decisions.if_no: You name the detail to change.

decisions.title: The reset-reason and boot-phase numbers
decisions.decision: ResetReason numbers: 0 unknown, 1 power-on, 2 watchdog (no record left), 3 reboot, 4 bootloader, 5 task-error budget, 6 supervisor starve-arm failed, 7 config reset, 8 FRAM erased, 9 command incomplete, 11-15 a boot that failed in phase 1-5, 20 C-stack exhaustion. Six boot phases are marked in RAM that survives a reset, once per transition, never in flash or FRAM.
decisions.why: You asked for a numeric code; the table is planned once and documented in the specification.

decisions.title: A rejected setting costs no flash write
decisions.decision: A setting is staged first and written to flash once after it was pushed to the chip. A push that fails and restores the old value writes nothing; a successful one writes once. The window in which a power loss loses the change grows by the push time.
decisions.why: Today a failed push can spend two flash writes for no net change, against your wear rule.
decisions.if_no: Write first, push second, as today.

decisions.title: The layer that detects a fault logs it; the others only print
decisions.decision: One fault leaves one entry in the persisted history: the layer that detects it persists the entry, the layers above only print to the console.
decisions.why: Read from your rule 'one event, one entry'; today one FRAM failure can leave three entries in the ring.
decisions.if_no: Every layer persists its own entry, as today.

decisions.title: Internal LED requests wait; REST LED commands are refused when busy
decisions.decision: Your rule refuses a REST LED command at once while a signal runs. An internal notification request instead waits for the running signal up to a deadline and then queues, as legacy queued it, but bounded.
decisions.why: Your answer covered the REST command; legacy's internal queueing is kept with a bound, so nothing is lost.
decisions.if_no: Internal requests are refused when busy too.

decisions.title: ISL29125: a failed threshold rewrite after a resolution change still reports success
decisions.decision: When a resolution change lands but the follow-up rewrite of the auto-range thresholds fails, the failure is logged and the setter still answers success.
decisions.why: The resolution itself took effect, and the next range switch or re-arm rewrites the thresholds.
decisions.if_no: The setter answers Failed although the resolution changed.

decisions.title: BMP3XX: a warning when the pressure offset leaves the formula's range
decisions.decision: If PressOffset moves pressure outside 300-1250 hPa, the reading is still published, sea-level pressure is left empty, and a warning is logged once.
decisions.why: It is a user setting, not a chip fault; you approved the fix, the warning is the planning's choice of signal.

decisions.title: Code values for the SGP40 and ISL29125 status fields
decisions.decision: VOCState: 0 blackout (first 46 samples), 1 learning (first 24 h after a fresh start), 2 settled, 3 restored from backup (first 24 h). CalLight: 0 not applicable now (fixed range or range changing), 1 suitable for calibration, 2 too dark, 3 too bright. The fourth CalLight code is the planning's addition.
decisions.why: You asked for numeric codes; the values follow the algorithm's own phases and the calibration band test.
decisions.if_no: You name other values or drop 'not applicable now'.

decisions.title: The settings write path moves into the base reader class
decisions.decision: The settings write path moves from the config-file reader class into the base reader class, so the SCD30 can use it with its chip-stored settings.
decisions.why: The config-file class cannot hold the SCD30's empty defaults, so it could not simply become one.
decisions.if_no: The SCD30 keeps its own separate write path.

decisions.title: Waits with no deadline poll at a slower idle rate
decisions.decision: Every poller waiting with no deadline uses a slower idle rate; for UDP that is 100 ms (the captive DNS listener), while waits inside a DNS or NTP exchange keep the 20 ms you confirmed.
decisions.why: The UART rule already does this; extended to every poller for consistency. The 100 ms is measured on the bench.
decisions.if_no: Only the UART keeps an idle rate.

decisions.title: The first NTP sync runs last at boot
decisions.decision: In the fixed boot order (construction, setup, tasks, timers), the first NTP force sync comes last, so the web server already answers while the sync runs.
decisions.why: Legacy also synced last; the placement is the planning's on that basis.
decisions.if_no: The sync runs before the tasks start, and the web server waits for it.

decisions.title: A flash erase may cost the UART link one frame
decisions.decision: On dev, a flash erase during a config flush runs with interrupts off and can overrun the UART's 32-byte receive FIFO: the link loses one frame and resyncs. This is accepted as degradation, not designed away.
decisions.why: It is a fault class the protocol already recovers from, and it happens only while a setting is being saved.
decisions.if_no: You ask for a design that never loses a frame during a flash erase.

decisions.title: Bounds for routine stalls and I2C timeouts
decisions.decision: Routine product computation may hold the loop for at most the 21 ms garbage-collection term, and an I2C bus timeout stays below half of the device's smallest hard consumer.
decisions.why: Both follow from measured worst cases.

decisions.title: The board's heap bounds keep their strength
decisions.decision: The heap bounds checked after a full system build on the board (largest free block at least 32,768 B, survivors at most 100,000 B, nothing placed in the top 16,384 B) stay as they are; each states its basis and changes only through a new derivation of the need, never to fit a reading.
decisions.why: You retired only the older floors; your rule asks tuned values to track measurements, while the earlier text forbade re-deriving these. The conservative reading keeps the check's strength.
decisions.if_no: The bounds follow each new measurement.

decisions.title: Your work-in-progress code counts as your later intent
decisions.decision: Code you committed in the old work-in-progress folder is read as your later intent when judging legacy parity, unless it defeats its own purpose.
decisions.why: It is the best evidence of your intent where no owner row exists.
decisions.if_no: Only legacy and owner rows count.

decisions.title: No driver re-stamps an old reading as new
decisions.decision: Your rule that a reading never claims a freshness it lacks binds every driver; the SCD30's 'no new data' reuse stays the one named exception with your reason.
decisions.why: The planning generalised your SCD30-specific rule.

decisions.title: SGP40 identity check kept and the serial read completed
decisions.decision: The SGP40 chip-identity check stays (it was observed on silicon), and the serial number read is completed to all three words; it is verified on the dev board.
decisions.why: An adaptation with no functional loss.

decisions.title: Bench sessions refuse to start from a non-standard board
decisions.decision: A bench session that finds the board outside its standard state (image, debug level, SCD30 values, FRAM write-protect, scratch files) fails at the start; repairing it is an opt-in flag.
decisions.why: A repair writes to flash; doing it silently would spend wear you did not plan.

decisions.title: Every hardware round starts and ends in a standard board state
decisions.decision: Every round ends on the release dev image with the error counts saved, debug level 5, the SCD30 at its configured values, FRAM write-protect clear and no scratch files, checked by fixtures at its end and the next round's start. This replaces the hand-kept board-state line.
decisions.why: A timed-out host call leaves a device script running; without a defined state the next test inherits it.
decisions.if_no: The board state stays a hand-kept note.

decisions.title: The console-starvation check becomes a gated bench test
decisions.decision: The check that a host holding the USB port open without reading does not starve the device becomes a gated bench test; it spends 2 flash writes (debug level set to 0 and back to 5).
decisions.why: A test makes the row repeatable instead of a hand step.
decisions.if_no: It stays a hand step in the wear round.

decisions.title: How the five hand-run hardware rows are measured
decisions.decision: Five hardware rows with no test get concrete hand steps: blocking NTP on the bench network to watch the SGP40 log, timing 100 reads per driver, timing LED ramps from the console, reading recovery-rung counts from the default run, and, only if planned, a temporary image without the 100 ms hotspot settle (2 flash cycles, reverted at once).
decisions.why: Their actions named the measurement but no instrument.

decisions.title: The twin's clean-boot check tolerates NTP being offline
decisions.decision: The twin's normal-boot log check tolerates exactly NTP's 'cannot resolve' and 'no reply' codes, and only while that boot's NTP is not synced, instead of running a local NTP server.
decisions.why: The offline twin cannot sync; the reason is stated where the tolerance sits.
decisions.if_no: A local NTP responder is built for the twin.

decisions.title: Type-only code is stripped by a line-preserving text edit
decisions.decision: The build removes type-checking-only blocks from the frozen image with a text edit that keeps every line in place, instead of rewriting the file through Python's ast module.
decisions.why: It handles every form, keeps the source line numbers in field tracebacks and removes the build's dependence on the host Python version.

decisions.title: The MicroPython stub releases are pinned by hand
decisions.decision: The stub package's exact post-release is pinned in versions.toml and checked against the MicroPython version, replacing CLAUDE.md's 'auto-derived, not a separate hand-kept pin'.
decisions.why: A stub post-release can change type results without a MicroPython change; a pin makes that visible.
decisions.if_no: Stubs stay auto-derived from the MicroPython version.

decisions.title: The comment-cap check counts long lines by length
decisions.decision: The 3-line comment cap counts a long comment line as several lines at a 110-character wrap; 84 existing blocks go over and are rewrapped in the same change.
decisions.why: Otherwise one very long line could hold a whole paragraph and pass your cap.
decisions.if_no: A line counts as one line whatever its length.

decisions.title: CI compares website changes against the last green run
decisions.decision: The website CI jobs decide whether to run by comparing against the last commit whose CI run succeeded, not just the previous push.
decisions.why: A push after a red run would otherwise skip the website tests for changes that were never tested green.
decisions.if_no: Compare against the default branch's merge base.

decisions.title: The bench installer checks sudo rights but never writes them
decisions.decision: The bench-tier installer checks and lists the passwordless sudo rules it needs (nmcli, iw, iptables, tc, tee, picotool, timeout, systemd-run, systemctl) but never writes a sudoers file.
decisions.why: Changing sudoers is a security setting on your machine; checking is the more reversible option.
decisions.if_no: The installer writes the sudoers file itself.

decisions.title: The bench Wi-Fi password stays off the command line
decisions.decision: The bench access-point password comes from an environment variable and is set through nmcli's interactive edit mode, never on the command line or in a log. If that mode does not read piped commands on the bench Pi, the fallback is recorded as a known limitation.
decisions.why: A password on a command line is visible to every process.

decisions.title: The written threat-model table
decisions.decision: The specification gains a table of every exposure (HTTP server, hotspot, captive DNS, NTP, UDP, USB, ...), the modes in which it exists and its disposition, under the trusted-home-LAN model you chose.
decisions.why: The plan's quality measure for security asks for your sign-off on the table itself.
decisions.if_no: You correct a row or a disposition.

decisions.title: Licence notices for derived code
decisions.decision: The captive DNS file carries 'Apache-2.0 AND MIT', scoping Apache-2.0 to the derived DNS-query class. A published image's notices include Sensirion's BSD-3-Clause text for the VOC algorithm as well as DFRobot's MIT terms. If the original captive-DNS repository is unreachable, its unsourced year is dropped rather than kept.
decisions.why: One notice more costs nothing; an unsourced year is not kept as fact.
decisions.if_no: Only the governing licence is named.

decisions.title: Moving your in-service WoZi unit is your own operation
decisions.decision: The rule 'WoZi is never flashed' binds sessions and the test tiers; moving your in-service WoZi unit to the new firmware is your operation, and the runbook says so.
decisions.why: Your earlier answers say reflashing a physical unit is yours.
decisions.if_no: The runbook stays silent on WoZi.

decisions.title: Every action needing a person in one section
decisions.decision: DEVICE_REFERENCE.md gets one commissioning and operating section listing every action that needs a person, with its trigger: Wi-Fi setup through the hotspot, the first AmbPres PUT that starts the SCD30, forced recalibration, ISL29125 calibration, reading the reset reason, and the reflash runbook.
decisions.why: Today these are spread over several docs.

decisions.title: The legacy favicon comes back without an extra connection
decisions.decision: The legacy icon returns as a 16x16 image embedded in the page, so loading the page still opens only two connections.
decisions.why: A separate favicon file would cost a connection on a device limited to six.

decisions.title: How timestamps, codes and numbers show on the website
decisions.decision: Timestamps show as ages (seconds below 120 s, minutes below 120 min, hours below 48 h, then days; 'clock mismatch' below -5 s). LastTaskEnd shows '<Task> at uptime <n> s', 'invalid value' or '-'. Status codes appear as clickable numbers that show their description. A number is accepted only in plain decimal form; anything else is sent as typed and the device answers Invalid. ContMeas shows no state until you set it (its default-value mechanism goes). CalLight colours follow a fixed tone table. The SCD30 temperature offset's hint names its 0.01 °C resolution. Special-value meanings show in the hint of number fields only; a 'modules without data' line appears only when there are some.
decisions.why: Each is the planning's choice inside your 'don't change the look' rule.
decisions.if_no: You name the detail to change.

decisions.title: A backup with a negative age is rejected
decisions.decision: An SGP40 backup whose timestamp lies in the future (negative age) is treated as expired, not accepted.
decisions.why: The conservative, reversible reading.
decisions.if_no: A negative age passes as fresh.

decisions.title: No GCC 14 leg in CI
decisions.decision: CI gets no GCC 14 build leg and the distribution compiler stays unpinned; your manual two-chroot check covers it.
decisions.why: You made that check a periodic owner-run one.
decisions.if_no: A GCC 14 CI job is added.

decisions.title: The frozen image is reproducible
decisions.decision: The same commit, pinned toolchain and pinned host Python give byte-identical frozen inputs and the same module order in the image; the frozen website is compressed without a name or time stamp.
decisions.why: Two identical builds should give identical firmware.
decisions.if_no: Builds may differ by file order or timestamps.

decisions.title: Long uptime and clock steps are proven in the test tiers
decisions.decision: Months of uptime (tick wraps, NTP cadence, counter decay, log-ring saturation) and forward/backward clock steps (first sync, offset change, DST) are proven under a driven clock in the unit and twin tiers for every device, not only by real-time soaks.
decisions.why: A gap the planning found in its own pillars.
decisions.if_no: These stay covered only by the soak and rollover runs.

decisions.title: A test that passes only on retry is never a plain pass
decisions.decision: A test file that passed only on its retry is named and counted in the summary and logged as an item to root-cause; the retry itself stays.
decisions.why: A retry can hide a real flake.

decisions.title: Hardware scripts run in the twin first
decisions.decision: A committed runner runs every device script and hardware test once against the twin before it enters the hardware queue, and again after a change to it or the API it calls; exceptions are listed.
decisions.why: You asked for a twin run before the queue; the committed runner and its trigger are the planning's.
decisions.if_no: The twin pre-run stays a scratch tool.

decisions.title: Test-only device-file keys are build metadata
decisions.decision: Device-file keys read only by tests and the bench harness (bench, hardware_family) count as build metadata, outside your 'no test-only artefacts' rule, because they never reach the image.
decisions.why: The rule targets product code.
decisions.if_no: Those facts move out of the device files.

decisions.title: Every setup() reports success
decisions.decision: Every class's setup() returns True or False, including the Wi-Fi service and the web server.
decisions.why: One contract lets the one setup runner treat every module alike.
decisions.if_no: setup() keeps returning nothing in some classes.

decisions.title: One readiness flag per class with a setup
decisions.decision: Every class with an async setup carries an 'initialized' flag, the reader base class, FRAM manager, web server, UART link driver, NeoPixel driver and notification service included; no method guards on it.
decisions.why: The register's construction/setup rule; the lead's later rulings replace an earlier exemption reading.
decisions.if_no: Those classes stay exempt from the readiness check.

decisions.title: One timeout helper
decisions.decision: Every wait that can be bounded uses one helper, wait_for_ms.
decisions.why: One mechanism instead of several hand-written ones.
decisions.if_no: Modules keep their own timeout code.

decisions.title: FRAM lock and status waits get no timeout
decisions.decision: Waits for the FRAM lock and status polls get no timeout: they wait only on this program's own tasks, and the watchdog stays the backstop.
decisions.why: A timeout there could only fire on a bug the watchdog already covers.
decisions.if_no: A timeout is added to these waits.

decisions.title: Readers declare their read triggers
decisions.decision: Each reader declares its read triggers through one method, from which the boot code starts them.
decisions.why: One declared list instead of hand wiring per reader.

decisions.title: One comment form per function
decisions.decision: Every Python scope explains a function the same way, with '#' comments.
decisions.why: One form per scope, extended from src/ to every Python scope.

decisions.title: One sleep form for every firmware sleep
decisions.decision: The float-sleep rule covers every sleep in the firmware, not only recurring ones, so its check needs no exception list.
decisions.why: A rule with no exceptions is simpler to check.
decisions.if_no: Only recurring sleeps follow the rule.

decisions.title: Attributes nothing outside reads become private
decisions.decision: Attributes and methods with no reader outside their class get a leading underscore across the core, network, UART and sensor classes; locks, 'initialized', names and public setters stay as they are.
decisions.why: The register's 'private by default' rule, applied by a scan of the code.

decisions.title: Methods only tests used are removed
decisions.decision: stop_uptime_timer(), set_debug_level() and the write-only timers_running flag go; tests reach the same behaviour from outside, through the REST path.
decisions.why: Your rule: code that exists only for tests is removed and the test rebuilt from outside.

decisions.title: Typed value checks
decisions.decision: Values are checked by checked_int(), checked_float() and checked_numeric(), each returning the value or None; runtime type checks that can never fire are not written.
decisions.why: The lead's ruling: a check that can never fire is dead code; the fix belongs at the type level.
decisions.if_no: One generic validator with runtime narrowing.

decisions.title: A named type for setup functions
decisions.decision: Setup functions get one named type, used by the setup runner and the generated boot code.
decisions.why: The existing callback type cannot describe a setup that returns a bool.
decisions.if_no: The setup list stays loosely typed.

decisions.title: Task names are always passed
decisions.decision: start_tasks() always takes the task names; there is no default.
decisions.why: A default would exist only for tests.

decisions.title: The C-stack entry uses a shared error number
decisions.decision: The C-stack log entry uses shared error number 25, because the system module's own number band is full.
decisions.why: Shared numbers exist for events any module can log.

decisions.title: The storage unpause waits for nothing once a reset is armed
decisions.decision: The task that ends a storage pause does nothing once a reset is armed or the shutdown sequence owns the watchdog.
decisions.why: Resuming writes during a shutdown would defeat the sequence.

decisions.title: A stack overflow uses the budget escalation
decisions.decision: The C-stack escalation reuses the task-budget escalation: check watchdog ownership again, feed once, stop feeding, reboot.
decisions.why: One escalation path, already proven for the error budget.
decisions.if_no: A second escalation path is written.

decisions.title: Marking the clock valid takes no argument
decisions.decision: set_utc_valid() takes no argument; it only ever marks the clock valid.
decisions.why: It has one caller and one meaning.

decisions.title: SCD30's config log stays RAM-only through a class attribute
decisions.decision: A class attribute keeps the SCD30's config log RAM-only, without a ninth constructor parameter.
decisions.why: Your 'no extra FRAM chunk' for the SCD30, within the eight-parameter limit.

decisions.title: Where the stack-overflow recorder lives
decisions.decision: The helper that records a stack overflow lives in the logging module, which every handler can import.
decisions.why: An import cycle rules out the base-classes module.

decisions.title: CRC helpers take the checked polynomial
decisions.decision: The CRC helpers take the already-checked polynomial as a parameter, so the code type-checks without an assert or an ignore comment.
decisions.why: Removes an assert from product code.

decisions.title: A CRC with an invalid polynomial passes data through
decisions.decision: A CRC object built with an out-of-range polynomial degrades to pass-through (length 0), as its documented contract already says.
decisions.why: The lead followed the documented contract; tests carry the cases.

decisions.title: A reset flushes settings before pausing FRAM
decisions.decision: The reset path flushes pending settings first, then pauses FRAM.
decisions.why: Settings reach flash before storage is closed.

decisions.title: Only ResetErrors: true is accepted
decisions.decision: A ResetErrors value other than true answers Invalid.
decisions.why: The specification documents only true.

decisions.title: Reading a blank FRAM block writes nothing
decisions.decision: A read of a blank FRAM block skips the busy marker, so it writes nothing (a blank setup drops from 74 to 54 chip-select cycles).
decisions.why: Nothing is read from a blank block, so the marker has nothing to protect.
decisions.if_no: Mark busy, then write the blank value back.

decisions.title: Small wording choices in core files
decisions.decision: A comment on delete_file() for the SCD30's memory, 'checks' instead of 'detects' in the FRAM driver, the response-envelope header without history, one header rewrite done earlier with its file's other changes, '2-degree' in the colour-temperature comment.
decisions.why: Comments state current facts.
decisions.if_no: You name the wording to change.

decisions.title: A standing check against blocking sleeps
decisions.decision: A host check fails on any blocking sleep in the firmware outside two named cases: the SPI chip-select settle and the boot-time bus clear.
decisions.why: Your rule that every rule keeps a guard; the old guard was an audit review that ends with the audit.

decisions.title: Unreachable guards go
decisions.decision: Two construction guards that no input can reach are removed from the DNS resolver and the NTP fetch.
decisions.why: Your rule removes unreachable branches.

decisions.title: NTP timing values in one object
decisions.decision: The NTP client's timing defaults live in one timing object; one unused timeout constant is deleted.
decisions.why: One place for the values the twin and tests also read.

decisions.title: Where the host-name check lives
decisions.decision: The host-name check lives in the DNS client, beside the address parser.
decisions.why: Both belong to name resolution.

decisions.title: One NTP error text covers parse failures
decisions.decision: Error 69 reads 'the reply is malformed or could not be parsed', since an allocation failure now lands there too.
decisions.why: The message must say what is logged.

decisions.title: Captive DNS back-off ids in milliseconds
decisions.decision: The captive DNS back-off tuning ids end in _ms, matching their converted unit.
decisions.why: One unit per id.

decisions.title: Test-only Wi-Fi parameters go
decisions.decision: The Wi-Fi service's GPIO-LED and refresh-rate parameters, used only by tests, are removed rather than made settable in the device file; host name and hotspot password become required keywords.
decisions.why: Your rule against test-only code.
decisions.if_no: The LED pin becomes a device-file setting.

decisions.title: The Wi-Fi LED setting's fallback
decisions.decision: If the LED setting cannot be read, the Wi-Fi LED follows its schema default.
decisions.why: A missing setting must not leave the LED undefined.

decisions.title: Captive DNS teardown warning gets a shared code
decisions.decision: The captive DNS server's teardown warning moves to a shared warning number; its old number stays unassigned.
decisions.why: The same event is shared across modules.

decisions.title: Two new error codes
decisions.decision: A captive DNS bind failure logs error 10 (INIT) and an NTP request that could not be sent logs new error 72.
decisions.why: Each event gets its own code.

decisions.title: Two branches kept on purpose
decisions.decision: The UDP socket's POLLERR branch and the Wi-Fi LED push's narrowing are kept, each with its reason stated.
decisions.why: Both can be reached on hardware.

decisions.title: Local socket faults stop at the retry step
decisions.decision: A fault on the device's own socket is handled by retrying, without escalating further up the recovery ladder.
decisions.why: A local socket fault has no participant to reset.
decisions.if_no: It escalates like a bus fault.

decisions.title: NTP lock-hold bound recorded
decisions.decision: The NTP client's lock-hold bound and the cases judged harmless are recorded with their reasons.
decisions.why: A recorded bound can be checked.

decisions.title: A Wi-Fi task restart in hotspot mode
decisions.decision: A Wi-Fi task restart in hotspot mode leaves the hotspot and starts a fresh connect streak, as legacy did; a permanently deactivated radio stays off until a power cycle.
decisions.why: Legacy behaviour, documented correctly.

decisions.title: LED command checks move into the web server
decisions.decision: The LED command's four value ranges move from generated code into the web server, next to the pause-time check they mirror.
decisions.why: One place validates every dispatch command.

decisions.title: /status keeps both IP and IPv4
decisions.decision: The networking section keeps both the IP and the IPv4 keys.
decisions.why: Both fit the key scheme (IPv4 is the standard spelling), and no change asked to remove either.
decisions.if_no: One of the two is removed in the key pass.

decisions.title: The web server retries a failed start
decisions.decision: If the server cannot start listening, it retries 3 times, 5 s apart, before its task ends and the supervisor restarts it.
decisions.why: The attempts span one full 10 s close linger, so a passing condition no longer costs a restart from the error budget.
decisions.if_no: A failed start ends the task at once, as today.

decisions.title: One function for the current UTC time
decisions.decision: Every module takes the current UTC time from one function with one 'not available' value, taken outside the sensor read's error handling.
decisions.why: Several hand-written copies of the same expression exist today; your 'one material' rule.
decisions.if_no: Each module keeps its own copy.

decisions.title: New UART log numbers
decisions.decision: Two new UART log codes are 91 (poll rate) and 92 (codec size); an earlier '91' for another event is read as a slip for 89.
decisions.why: Next free numbers in the band.

decisions.title: UART attributes private from the first rename
decisions.decision: UART attributes no outside code reads become private in the first renaming unit, and all later UART work uses the private names.
decisions.why: Keeps the changelog's numbering and avoids renaming twice.

decisions.title: No coroutine per received frame
decisions.decision: The valid-frame bookkeeping becomes a plain function, so a received frame no longer allocates a coroutine.
decisions.why: Its only await is gone; no per-frame allocation.

decisions.title: UART task starter names
decisions.decision: The UART starters are named start_asy_listen and start_asy_exercise.
decisions.why: They meet the starter naming rule.

decisions.title: The exerciser banner stays a constant
decisions.decision: The link exerciser's banner stays a compile-time constant; the test reads it from source.
decisions.why: No test-only export.

decisions.title: A resync logs once
decisions.decision: A resync either persists its warning or prints its routine line, never both.
decisions.why: One event, one entry.

decisions.title: The link driver keeps its own readiness flag
decisions.decision: The UART link driver keeps its own 'initialized' flag, which its exercise loop reads.
decisions.why: The loop needs it.
decisions.if_no: It uses the comm object's flag.

decisions.title: The bench exerciser banner is renamed
decisions.decision: The dev-only exerciser's banner text is renamed under the no-variant rule, logged as a Python-internal changelog line.
decisions.why: An application payload, not protocol.

decisions.title: VOC algorithm catches only struct errors
decisions.decision: The VOC algorithm's two handlers catch only the errors its struct calls raise, instead of importing the logging module into a pure algorithm file.
decisions.why: A stack overflow still reaches the SGP40 reader's handler, which records it.

decisions.title: The VOC port keeps its upstream order
decisions.decision: The literal port of the VOC algorithm is not reordered to the member-order rule.
decisions.why: It stays traceable line by line to its source.

decisions.title: Tuning ids drop '_default'
decisions.decision: Tuning-table ids drop the '_default' suffix once their values are fixed.
decisions.why: The suffix no longer means anything.

decisions.title: One name stem for the LED overlay state
decisions.decision: The NeoPixel overlay state uses one _overlay_* name stem.
decisions.why: One concept, one name.

decisions.title: Notification setup reports its config
decisions.decision: The notification service's setup returns whether its config store is valid; a refused signal is logged as a warning.
decisions.why: Setup reports success like every class.

decisions.title: BMP3XX sea-level pressure as a constant
decisions.decision: The BMP3XX's standard sea-level pressure becomes a named constant; its unreachable guard goes.
decisions.why: Named values, no dead code.

decisions.title: Two new shared warning names
decisions.decision: Shared warnings 11 and 12 are named DERIVED_DOMAIN and SOCKET_TEARDOWN.
decisions.why: Next free shared numbers.

decisions.title: BMP3XX re-apply returns a code
decisions.decision: Re-applying stored BMP3XX settings returns a result code; only the init routine declares an init failure.
decisions.why: One place decides failure.

decisions.title: One name for the shared read divider
decisions.decision: The shared read divider takes the name _trigger_loop().
decisions.why: The name the base-class change already uses.

decisions.title: SCD30 keeps its always-write list in firmware
decisions.decision: The SCD30's list of always-executed settings stays in the firmware, pinned by a host check to the website tags.
decisions.why: The firmware never reads the tags, which are comments.
decisions.if_no: It is derived from the tags at build time.

decisions.title: Where the SGP40 backup type lives
decisions.decision: The SGP40 backup record type lives in the SGP40 driver.
decisions.why: It is SGP40-specific.
decisions.if_no: It lives in a shared module.

decisions.title: ISL29125 re-arm flag resets on restart
decisions.decision: The ISL29125 interrupt re-arm flag is reset when its task restarts.
decisions.why: An episode never outlives its task.

decisions.title: ISL29125 interrupt park tests
decisions.decision: The ISL29125 interrupt park and re-arm are tested only on cycles without a range switch, with one writer of the armed flag.
decisions.why: A switch rewrites the same registers.

decisions.title: ISL29125 recovery step takes no settings lock
decisions.decision: The ISL29125 participant recovery step re-applies the chip's shadow without the settings lock.
decisions.why: It re-applies the shadow, not the file, unlike the BMP3XX and SCD30.

decisions.title: One optional-value check stays
decisions.decision: One 'counts is None' re-check in the ISL29125 driver stays under the convention for optional values.
decisions.why: The convention keeps it.

decisions.title: ISL29125 comments in present tense
decisions.decision: Four ISL29125 comments are restated in present tense.
decisions.why: Comments state current facts.

decisions.title: BMP3XX conversion wait from the datasheet
decisions.decision: The BMP3XX conversion wait is computed from the datasheet's measurement-time formula.
decisions.why: Derived, not guessed.

decisions.title: ISL29125 parks an interrupt the peak rule overrules
decisions.decision: The ISL29125 parks its interrupt when the peak rule overrules the window it watches.
decisions.why: An interrupt that cannot change the decision is noise.

decisions.title: MeanAtmTemp's lower bound becomes -40 °C
decisions.decision: The BMP3XX MeanAtmTemp setting accepts -40 to 50 °C instead of -50 to 50.
decisions.why: The smallest change that keeps every accepted value inside the formula's range; you approved the fix.
decisions.if_no: A wider range with values the formula rejects.

decisions.title: One name, one meaning for get_altitude()
decisions.decision: The BMP3XX's pressure-derived get_altitude() is renamed, since SCD30's get_altitude() means the configured altitude.
decisions.why: One name, one meaning.

decisions.title: The VOC algorithm is built at construction
decisions.decision: The SGP40's VOC algorithm object is built when the driver is constructed, not at the first read.
decisions.why: Its start reads no clock or bus, so the result is identical and the type is simpler.

decisions.title: I2C reads reuse one buffer view
decisions.decision: I2C register reads slice one long-lived view of the scratch buffer, and whole-buffer transfers pass the buffer directly.
decisions.why: Fewer allocations per read; the bytes on the wire are the same.

decisions.title: LED tasks start into a defined state
decisions.decision: Every LED task starts or restarts into a defined pixel state.
decisions.why: A restart must not leave a stale colour.

decisions.title: 0 is the one 'no timestamp' value for SGP40 backups
decisions.decision: BackupTS and RestoreTS use 0 for 'no timestamp' (replacing 0 for one and -1 for the other); null still means none since boot.
decisions.why: 0 is what the FRAM chunk already returns, and a real timestamp is never 0 once timestamps exist only after an NTP sync.

decisions.title: One boot-entry file name
decisions.decision: The generated boot entry is called sensortask_<device>_main.py for both the command line and the batch build.
decisions.why: Two names existed in the plan.

decisions.title: One poll-interval constant
decisions.decision: The website poll interval is one constant under one tuning id.
decisions.why: One value, one tag.

decisions.title: dev.toml crossover comment rewrapped
decisions.decision: The crossover comment in dev.toml is tightened to three lines within 100 characters.
decisions.why: The comment cap.

decisions.title: Wording of the page's new header
decisions.decision: The wording of index.html's new header comment.
decisions.why: Every file opens with one header.

decisions.title: The no-autostart entry names the manual-start options
decisions.decision: The no-autostart boot entry's comment names main()'s other keywords.
decisions.why: They are the documented manual-start options.

decisions.title: Name of the no-autostart image
decisions.decision: The no-autostart build writes build/firmware-<device>-noautostart.uf2 and prints the manual start line.
decisions.why: You asked for the option; the name and banner are the planning's.

decisions.title: A 'hidden' website tag key
decisions.decision: The website tag grammar gains a hidden= key.
decisions.why: Some fields are published but not shown.

parked.title: Chunking large UART allocations
parked.why_parked: You deferred it (2026-09-26). The UART code allocates from the peer-declared size (up to 64,770 bytes) and a line reader grows without bound; both catch the out-of-memory error, which your memory rule counts as a design defect. It stays in BACKLOG's question list with the options: chunk both, cap by a declared size, or keep as a documented exception.
